summary: Phase B Design System frontend testing: unified RoleLayout, mobile bottom nav, OTP 6-box input, form styling. Logged in as all 3 roles on desktop+mobile (1440x900 and 390x844). OTP auto-advance/backspace/paste all pass. 2 real bugs found: (1) Platform Owner accent color NOT applied due to class name mismatch, (2) Stat cards on /platform and /admin dashboards still use legacy 'card' class instead of '.stat-card' with role accent border as required.

ui_bugs.issue: Platform Owner accent color (#534AB7 purple) is NOT applied. PlatformLayout.js passes role='platform_owner' which produces CSS class 'role-platform_owner', but index.css only defines '.role-platform' (no '_owner' suffix). As a result, Platform Owner falls back to the :root default accent (#185FA5 admin blue) — brand icon, active sidebar items, stat-card border-left, buttons, and OTP focus ring all render blue instead of purple. Visually confirmed: platform dashboard brand icon is blue. Fix options: either change class naming (role='platform' in PlatformLayout.js) or add '.role-platform_owner' block to index.css (and also add '.role-sub_admin' vs '.role-sub-admin' — current index.css uses '.role-sub_admin' so sub_admin is OK).

Stat cards use legacy className='card p-6' instead of the new '.stat-card' class specified in Phase B requirements. The new class adds role-accent left border (3px) and proper typography. Currently cards appear as plain white cards with no accent indicator. 0 .stat-card elements found on /admin and /platform dashboards.

issues: Brand icon, accent color, and any active/hover accents are all blue (#185FA5) instead of purple (#534AB7) — role theme broken.
Stat cards have no role-accent left border; appear as flat white cards.
Stat cards do not use .stat-card class — missing left-border accent, not matching Phase B typography spec.

Either (a) change PlatformLayout.js line 15 to role='platform' (and update data-testid expectations), OR (b) add a CSS rule '.role-platform_owner { --accent: 249 43% 50%; --accent-raw: #534AB7; --accent-light: #EEEDFE; --accent-dark: #26215C; }' in /app/frontend/src/index.css (around line 50). Recommend option (b) to avoid breaking other usages. Verify Platform dashboard brand icon and active sidebar item turn purple after fix.

critical_code_review_comments: Class naming mismatch between JS (role-${role}) and CSS (.role-platform) is fragile — no lookup table, no test. Recommend documenting the role→class mapping or centralizing.
Stat card migration to .stat-card class was incomplete — only CSS was added but JSX was not updated. This is a common Phase B oversight.
RoleLayout.js is 384 lines, borderline OK but consider splitting DesktopSidebar / MobileDrawer / MoreSheet / BottomNav into sub-components for maintainability.

'Made with Emergent' fixed badge overlaps bottom-right content on mobile (390x844) and intercepted pointer events in some test flows — environmental, not a code issue, but bottom nav pb safe-area seems OK.

rca of the issue: Platform Owner accent mismatch RCA: RoleLayout.js line 66 generates className using template literal `role-${role}`. PlatformLayout.js passes role='platform_owner' (matching backend role value), producing class 'role-platform_owner'. However index.css line 50 defines only '.role-platform' (shortened form). When the expected CSS rule doesn't match, CSS variables fall back to :root scope (line 11: --accent-raw: #185FA5). All 4 color roles should be consistently named — admin/sub_admin/resident currently work because their role values happen to match CSS class names. Reproduction: login as 9999999999/owner123, inspect body — class='role-platform_owner' but document.body getComputedStyle returns --accent-raw: #185FA5. Mitigation: add '.role-platform_owner' CSS block mirroring '.role-platform' values.
